experiments.name: Multi-agent throughput
experiments.hypothesis: running six agents in parallel produces more than running one
experiments.method: six lanes against a solo baseline, preregistered, sum of per-lane durations
experiments.result: 1.08x the output for 3.2x the compute, 955 agent-seconds against 297
experiments.note: write-up lives in fleet-ops, which is private. The tool and its findings are public at github.com/Morkeeth/fleet; this specific measurement is not yet.

experiments.name: Harness premium, Terminal-Bench 2.1
experiments.hypothesis: a model's native scaffold beats a model-agnostic reference harness
experiments.method: every pair on the public 2.1 leaderboard where one model runs under both, delta over the combined error bar
experiments.result: not constant and not the same sign. Gemini CLI is 8.1 points BELOW Terminus 2 on the same model; Codex is 5.1 above; two of five pairs are noise
experiments.note: RE-ANALYSIS of someone else's leaderboard, not an experiment I ran. It becomes mine the day I run Terminus 2 myself.

experiments.name: Does tailoring a document to its reader help?
experiments.hypothesis: a document rewritten for one specific reader beats the untouched original
experiments.method: 54 blind judges, three repeats per variant, one sentence changed at a time and everything else byte-identical
experiments.result: the tailored version scored lower and five times less stably, spread 0.83 against 0.17. Replicated three days apart on independent runs
experiments.note: run on my own instrument. Write-up is in a private repo.

experiments.name: Dip-buy rule, walk-forward
experiments.hypothesis: the dip-buy rule has an edge out of sample
experiments.result: no out-of-sample edge. Median held-out trade minus 50.3% of margin, n=9 and 5
experiments.note: underpowered and stated as such. It does not prove the rule is dead, only that there is no evidence it is alive. The strategy was shelved; the risk engine was kept.

trackNotes.agents: most of these were hackathon experiments, shaped by the bounty text and the sponsor list rather than by a problem I had. three were not: BriefMCP, Loop and Taste Machine.
trackNotes.hackathons: the prize money is stated at time of win and never re-priced. what happened to it afterwards is a position, not a prize, and it is a different page.

projects.name: Ledger
projects.oneLiner: roadmaps, POCs, a send-performance harness, testing suites for clear signing, and the specifications for new features. a lot of architectural work on how things are supposed to work, for users and for the features themselves. mostly it is research distilled into what the hell can we do with this, how can it touch end users, and how can it move the needle. embedded apps, backend teams, nodes, infra.

projects.name: Anotherblock
projects.oneLinerSource: Oscar, 2026-08-16, verbatim; Onchain Summer dates verified at source
projects.oneLiner: it was insanity. legal engineering of what even makes sense, and pitching almost free money to artists. they have so much unpublished material, progress that never sees the light. royalties are the more legal side; now they could sell their drafts, which was not mainstream or polished yet. we called all night pitching the new concept until we had a line-up, then worked on artwork and what else could be given. it put us on day six of Coinbase's Onchain Summer, 14 August 2023, the day after Coca-Cola, with never-before-heard tracks from Boys Noize and Laidback Luke. difficult to scale, though - like luxury you need scarcity and rarity, and an mp3 file just is not that.

projects.name: Etablera
projects.oneLiner: delivering projects end to end, managing expectations, negotiating, and learning that saying no helps. cheap clients and early annoyance lead to more of it later, not less. product marketing is the core of understanding what users want, and video editing and campaign launches are essential to knowing how things look and which angle to push. and organising hackathons and events is energetic.

projects.name: Wave Radio
projects.oneLiner: a way to channel my thoughts, and one of my favourite mediums. I host it with Erik Nilsson and Eric Zackariason, and it lets me ask people hey, want to join my podcast. it ages well - a snapshot of what we were thinking. the ongoing obsession is whether it should be short format, and not wanting it to get too famous. it is almost an art project.

projects.name: RELAY → FAVOUR
projects.oneLiner: post a real-world favour and a World ID verified human goes and does it, with photo proof an AI checks. it got a couple of users and then stalled on not being accepted. I tried to stimulate usage by putting money in, but the agentic-bounty, rent-a-human idea did not really make sense for that audience - the World app store is used mostly by people in Nigeria and the Philippines who are there for quick tokens. next step is either real collaboration with the World Foundation, or a completely new app tailored to who is actually there.

projects.name: Yieldbound
projects.oneLiner: agents do not need full wallets, they need bounded authority: lock the principal and let the agent spend only what the yield earns. silver from MoonPay. my first agentic hackathon and it was amazing - pushed by odawg and Bagel, and a lot of the best stories came out of it. probably frozen now.

projects.name: RECEIPT
projects.oneLiner: signed, hash-linked receipts for agent work, then a score of whether the work was actually useful - an agent cannot pick its own grader. built for ETHGlobal Online on OG. top 20, won nothing, and honestly it was mainly a cool demo: hard to use in my own setup.

projects.name: BriefMCP
projects.oneLiner: sharing context inside a team. an MCP server holding the context files on a RAG, so they can be retrieved independently of the harness - from Claude Code to Cursor and back.

projects.name: People Radar
projects.oneLiner: I have always wanted to keep track of contacts and people, in one chat interface. building it taught me that most of it comes up naturally anyway, which is why recall is nice to have rather than urgent.

projects.name: The OS
projects.oneLiner: the second brain, and the operating system it runs on.

projects.name: Loop
projects.oneLiner: calendar events, and a dream Erik Nilsson and I had. put one magical event in your calendar, get a weekly brief narrated by ElevenLabs, and an eval on which kinds of events are actually worth going to.

projects.name: Gates
projects.oneLiner: token-gated feature unlocking. a developer tool that gates features and experiences by what a user holds.

projects.name: ArbiGates
projects.oneLiner: an extension of Gates onto Arbitrum, gating video quality by what a user holds.

projects.name: NFT Safe Launch
projects.oneLiner: condition-gated release infrastructure. external data decides when something unlocks. not an NFT project.

projects.name: AAtomato
projects.oneLiner: onboarding to crypto payments. a bank account in ten seconds, unbanked to banked.

projects.name: Swosh.cash
projects.oneLiner: transfer control. protocol research into the approve-all pattern, so funds can be moved or off-ramped easily - and so everything can be pulled out at once in a security breach.

projects.name: Contrib
projects.oneLiner: joined Antler, pitched Contrib, a developer community for people contributing to DAOs. hacked it and won, then found out the community did not want an equity company, they wanted a token launch - so we ran a small membership instead, and I turned down the $95K to raise from the community rather than give up equity. then DAOs died. they did not work. I kept leading the community anyway: 800 discord members, 100 of them building across different organisations. it is still there, quieter now but alive. then anotherblock made more sense.

projects.name: Mount Helicon
projects.oneLiner: built for a Qwen and Alibaba hackathon, and frozen there. then I wanted my own tool, which is Mountain of Helicon - the one we actually use.

projects.name: KYA
projects.oneLiner: a security audit of other agents, paid for with x402 agentic payments on OKX's new agent store. results not back yet.

projects.name: Overturn
projects.oneLiner: the idea was to stop settling bets while a VAR review is still running - the phantom goal problem. it used the sponsor's tooling properly rather than decoratively. won nothing.

projects.name: Litmus
projects.oneLiner: a beautifully abstracted CRM: three top contacts scored every morning, each with a cited reason. I thought we had a real chance, and then five other teams had built the same thing. convergence, again.

projects.name: Taste Machine
projects.oneLiner: a simple evaluation and feedback engine for finding tweets and replies worth writing: tone of voice, and the right target.

projects.name: cline
projects.oneLinerSource: the PR body, verified against the repo
projects.oneLiner: their monorepo move left copilot-instructions routing at a deleted src/; of 19 routed paths 1 resolved. fixed the 11 with verifiable destinations, flagged the 9 without one rather than guess.

projects.name: Mountain of Helicon
projects.oneLinerSource: PyPI summary + a cold install, NEEDS VOICE PASS
projects.oneLiner: pip install mountain-of-helicon. audits agent-memory rot across a whole agent stack; 62 CLI subcommands and 23 MCP tools in the shipped wheel, and it killed two of its own findings the week it made them.

projects.name: fleet
projects.oneLiner: one of the most fascinating experiments I have run: taking multi-agent output seriously and setting the whole thing up agentically. the throughput hypothesis came back null, 1.08x the output for 3.2x the compute, and six findings a second agent could not reproduce were cut rather than softened.

projects.name: RETRACT
projects.oneLiner: compensating actions for agent work on CockroachDB and AWS Bedrock. six evals, each carrying its own control arm.

projects.name: Skill Issue
projects.oneLiner: first Kaggle entry, to the agent skill-lift benchmark. reported an honest null with its control arms instead of a lift claim, and retracted its own harm finding before the deadline. results pending, no placement.

projects.name: agent-attack
projects.oneLiner: an adversarial evaluation for the Kaggle AI Agent Security competition, multi-step tool attacks, 1,554 teams. submitted and scoring; not placed. repo still private.

projects.name: weirder-md
projects.oneLiner: six unusual ways to read a plain markdown file, and the live page rebuilds from git for someone who is not me.

projects.name: nullspace
projects.oneLiner: databases are built to store what is there. nullspace stores what was missing. every query that comes back empty gets filed, so you can see the shape of what people asked for and did not get. you ask the restaurant for a bottle of wine, they say no sir we do not have it, and nobody writes that down. this writes it down. built for datahub.

projects.name: pigeon
projects.oneLiner: API keys and env variables are a nightmare to hand around, and the models got sensitive about printing them in chat. the fix is a clipboard save, which I read on twitter and which nobody tells you. pigeon is the guided version for people new to vibe coding - one, two, three, and the key is in the native iCloud keychain for good.
